# Intended behaviour changes since v0.11.2

F-OVERRIDE: Recovery accurately reports family enforcement by default using a localizable message. An explicitly acknowledged override is separate from normal Flash. No default write behavior changes.

PROTO: brand-independent read-only protocol evidence replaces name/standard-feature gates. INQUIRY optical type, structured F1 and boot-banner reads establish a unique protocol; conflicting signatures are refused. Recovery retains Current-assisted blank-loader binding. No update-transfer or receiver-compatibility checks are relaxed. Exact changed transcripts are recorded below.

P6 (0.13.1): clearer pre-write errors and provenance-only backup messages; no device-command or safety-gate changes.

`tests/golden/v0.11.2/` holds the golden scenarios recorded with the same
harness against the v0.11.2 tag. `golden_parity_with_0_11_2` requires that
every difference is listed below, under its golden file and scenario, line
for line (`-` = only in v0.11.2, `+` = only now). A Pioneer scenario may
differ only for the Pioneer reasons below; a MediaTek scenario only for its listed reasons:

| id | reason |
|----|--------|
| OPERATION_015 | 0.15.0: confirmation prompts and accepted answers use the selected language; Pioneer requires a usable installed backup and never offers a bypass it cannot execute. Typed localized user issues retain pre-write and read-only evidence; internal error chains gain stable cause markers. Recovery states whether its family gate is retained or explicitly bypassed. Expected restart command failures remain in diagnostics rather than user warnings. Write ordering, payloads and verification comparisons are unchanged. |
| CLI_INFO | 0.14.4: CLI drive information groups and aligns the shared GUI identity, interface, capabilities, region and settings fields. GUI field values and device-command transcript remain unchanged. Native transport traces stay in diagnostics. |
| HUMAN_ERRORS | 0.14.1: optional DVD region, Pioneer identity and settings read failures show Unavailable. Full causes remain in English diagnostics. No device commands or values from successful reads change. |
| PRECHECK | 0.14.0: proven pre-write failures retain phase and no-write evidence; hardware mismatches have actionable model guidance with original family identifiers in diagnostics. Pioneer preview explicitly leaves installed compatibility pending. No SCSI commands, payloads, programming order or compatibility gates change. |
| FMT | Snapshot normalization removes trailing display padding, including empty structured `MSG` rows and terminal prompts. Commands, payload bytes, message content and assertions are unchanged; the historical v0.11.2 snapshots remain untouched. |
| P10 | Pioneer 0.13.4: the shared optical executor derives the dialect from decoded firmware, binds the live receiver before entry and again after startup migration, and checks target identity plus Kernel and available Normal readback after each pass. OEM vendor identity binds to the loaded firmware ID, and revisions compare the defined four-byte INQUIRY field (including the projected `0.05e` release). Recovery with a supplied Current envelope uses its decoded Kernel signatures, dialect and exact identity to establish an OEM receiver; unsupported probing without Current remains refused. Golden devices now install the transferred Normal, report its tag and revision, and expose programmed bytes for verification. Typed failures retain the underlying transport cause. The corpus also refreshes the earlier optical 0.15.1 receiver-derived `FrontKeyTwoRegion` framing (`6c8c2be`, `9100f74`, `5847fe4`): a 0x1200 Kernel header/key transfer followed by two 0x8000 body transfers at offsets 0x1200 and 0x9200. Flash already used this before the current audit; Recovery now shares that plan. Contiguous Kernel bytes, Normal transfers and control payloads are preserved. |
| P11 | Pioneer corpus refresh of the prior 0.13.1 Normal preparation fixes (`a20047a`, `3b2a421`, October 19): preserve a valid OEM representation or prepare Normal for its actual receiving Kernel, proving decoded-body equality and receiver-required authentication. The corpus snapshots were last refreshed on October 11 (`9ee1a1d`); valid Normal-only scenarios now reach execution. Authentication gates remain in force, and incompatible Kernel-version or corrupt-body cases still refuse. The 34 newly exercised locally signed Normal transfers use recorded valid authentication blocks in tests, keyed by receiver authentication policy and every byte outside the 0x170..0x1c0 signature/public-key block. Fresh and recorded signatures are both verified; full emitted wire digests remain asserted. Production signing remains random. |
| RECOVERY_TRAY | 0.14.5: Pioneer Recovery skips the Flash-only medium guard before its initial and restoration passes; ordinary Flash still rejects a loaded disc. The recorded Recovery execution transcripts omit those two medium-status checks. No write command, payload, ordering, family check or verification is relaxed. |
| M-LIFECYCLE | MediaTek 0.13.4: immutable receiver plans own authorization, encoding, execution and exact target startup verification. Plan messages describe the receiver-bound sequence; cached evidence is revalidated before entry. Successful mocks now expose the actual programmed descriptor and matching INQUIRY, and synthetic descriptors have a valid vendor and revision. Completion distinguishes verified readback from unavailable readback; structured errors preserve the failed phase and transport cause. |
| P9 | Pioneer 0.13.4: the UD04 golden mock now returns its real `GENERAL` Kernel tag from vendor identity so the firmware-derived entry preflight can match the captured installed Kernel. Only post-flash identity text in these mock transcripts changes; firmware write commands and payloads do not. |
| P8 | Pioneer 0.13.3: read the live A0 startup word 0x9F before firmware transfer, write and verify only when it differs from the target value, then continue. The added read and preflight commands in these mock transcripts reflect this migration; neutral FFFF already matches and sends no A0 write. |
| P7 | Pioneer 0.13.2: post-finish readiness polling sends REQUEST SENSE (`03 00 00 00 12 00`, allocation 18) before GET EVENT STATUS / TEST UNIT READY. The traced programming-busy guard admits REQUEST SENSE to the command-completion restart path while other commands can return early. Each successful mock pass adds exactly one read and increments the transcript count; two-pass restoration adds two. Firmware write commands and payloads are unchanged. This does not establish the separate persistent-startup-setting fix. |
| P1 | Pioneer: a package that cannot be read is refused at the plan, before the backup, so no backup file is saved and no `backup:` line is shown |
| P2 | Pioneer: the last tray check runs after the confirmation, right before the first write. A successful flash issues the same device commands. When authorize refuses (or the user declines), there is one fewer tray check. With a disc inserted after the backup, the `backup:` line, the confirmation text and the prompt appear before the refusal |
| P3 | Pioneer: a drive that does not identify as a BD or DVR generation is refused without the dead `--recover` hint. v0.11.2: `the drive does not identify as a BD or DVR generation (a guess is only made under --recover, for a recognised BD family); refusing before any write`; now: `the drive does not identify as a BD or DVR generation; refusing before any write` (954f51d). The hint named a flash mode no user could reach since 0.11.0: the CLI always passed `force: false` (v0.11.2 main.rs:198), the GUI forced it off (app.rs:292), and a forced Pioneer flash was refused anyway (workflow.rs:284). A P3 scenario may differ only by lines that drop the hint, so its device commands are identical |
| P4 | Pioneer: the synthetic Kernel test fixtures gained a receiver rotation decode-loop at Kernel offset `0x114` (an `AND.W #0x1F` key mask, a `MOV` of the count, and a shift-helper `JSR`), required by pioneer-optical 0.15.0, which refuses a Kernel whose Normal rotation direction is undetectable (`UnknownRotation`). The fixtures also gained a synthetic RAM-programmer handoff and startup signature for the generic Kernel replacement gate. Only fixture-derived bytes differ — the Kernel, backup and write-payload digests and the firmware fingerprint — while every device command, message and refusal is byte-identical. The Pioneer analogue of R8 |
| R1 | MT1939 / generic MediaTek backup rebuilt from the OEM catalog |
| R2 | always-on MT1959/MT1939 chip gate and its extra identity reads |
| R3 | raw-drive-read refusal |
| R4 | known-boot-page requirement |
| R5 | MediaTek `Chipset` info row |
| R6 | round-1 audit fixes (sanitized output, INVALID CMAC report, accurate enter_update message, lazy banner read) |
| R7 | mediatek-optical crate move (CDBs byte-identical; labels and refusal wording come from the shared engine/flashset) |
| R8 | the synthetic MediaTek fixtures carry a hardware configuration record (boot banner, descriptor platform code at `+0x46`, feature template and record at `0x11000`), which the hardware-family gate needs. Commands are unchanged; only the bytes that depend on the fixture differ: payload and file digests, the displayed banner, the firmware fingerprint and the first differing read-back offset |
| M-RS | MediaTek REQUEST SENSE (STATUS) is sent as the OEM updaters send it, `03 00 00 00 10 80` padded to 12 bytes: allocation length `0x10` in byte 4, `0x80` in the control byte. We sent `03 00 00 10 80 00`, one byte off. Evidence: LG's MT19xx updater v1.081 (`WH16NS40.exe`, sha256 `281c668c…806bac`, file offset `0x1383`) builds it as `c6 45 f0 03` / `66 c7 45 f4 10 80` (`cdb[0] = 03`, `cdb[4..6] = 10 80`); v1.074 (`BH16NS40(1.03-A0).exe`) the same with allocation `0x12`. Every other MT1959 command and payload is byte-identical |
| M-FAM | MediaTek same-hardware-family crossflash gate. v0.11.2 refused any image of another model by name; now an image of another model is admitted when it is the drive's hardware family (and refused, before any write, when it is not). A different-family dry run reads the drive's boot banner (its loader tells apart families that share a platform) and refuses with "this image is for a different hardware family" instead of the wrong-model message |
| M-CHIP | MediaTek chip generation (MT1959 vs MT1939) is now decided by the boot loader banner at 0x3000, never the stale `MTEKMT19xx` identity tag (which is shown only as a curiosity). Consequences visible in the goldens: the `chipset` line reads "from boot banner; identity tag …" (was "via identity string; tag …"); the `banner` row shows the real banner (the chip gate always reads it, so the SCSI transcript gains one `3c06…3000…2000` read even when the descriptor has a tag); a legacy `.tar` backup is described from its rebuilt image, so a synthetic fixture with no 0x3000 banner now reads as unrecognized rather than keying on the embedded tag; and an image/drive whose banner names the chip is labelled by that banner (an MT1939-tagged JB8 build is MT1959) |
| M-BAK | MediaTek backup/dump now probes for freemkv-modified firmware before reading: a READ BUFFER Identity knock (`3c 0e c0 de 01 00 00 00 60 00`, alloc 96) precedes the OEM read on every capture, so a drive already running freemkv firmware is read through its injected `DumpAll` command (stock MediaTek firmware exposes no full-flash read). The transcript gains one `3c0ec0de010000006000 alloc=96` read; on a stock/mock drive the reply is not the `freemkv` magic, so it falls through to the OEM read and the rest of the sequence is unchanged. Also: when a MediaTek pre-flash backup cannot be captured, the operator may consent to flash without one (every other gate still runs), so a declined/failed capture now aborts with "pre-flash backup failed and flashing without one was declined; aborting flash: <cause>" |
| P5 | Pioneer: when the pre-flash backup cannot be captured, the flow now offers to flash without a rollback backup; the default (non-interactive / scripted front-end) declines, so the abort message reads "pre-flash backup failed and flashing without one was declined; aborting flash: <cause>" (was the bare cause). No device commands change |

| M-ENC | Active MediaTek receiver detection adds INQUIRY and code reads during planning, a receiver/encoding plan field, and identity/code revalidation before writing. Executable authorization additionally reads the entry grammar and opcode/callback records after backup capture; the immutable library plan revalidates these before writing. Synthetic firmware contains plaintext receiver and positive entry/registration excerpts, changing fixture hashes; mock firmware identities correctly report optical peripheral type 5. The legacy receiver fixture retains every write CDB, direction, length and outcome. |

The baseline set was produced by copying `src/golden_tests.rs` into a
`git worktree` of the v0.11.2 tag and changing only its COMPAT shims
(`mtk_boot_page`, `recover_via`, the `flash_plan` import); blessing it there
writes the files in `v0.11.2/`.

**Removed scenarios.** removed: unreachable path deleted in phase 1 (CLI
main.rs passes force:false; GUI app.rs forces false). These scenarios drove
`FlashRequest.{force, skip_backup, recover}` directly and were dropped from
both the current and the v0.11.2 sets:

* flash_execute.txt: `MTK execute: --skip-backup`, `MTK execute: --force (no
  backup)`, `Pioneer execute: --force, no backup, no installed receiver`,
  `Pioneer execute: --skip-backup`
* mtk_flash_input_refusals.txt: the five `MTK dry run: … (--force)` variants
* pioneer_plan_and_gates.txt: the `recover` and `force` variants of every
  `resolve_flash_plan: installed=…` scenario (the `plain` ones remain)
* pioneer_flash_bundle_failures.txt: `Pioneer flash_bundle: --recover`,
  `Pioneer flash_bundle: --force`

removed in phase 3: `FlashRequest.allow_crossflash` was always false (the CLI
and GUI never set it), so its waiver was unreachable and is deleted. The one
scenario that set it was dropped from both sets:

* flash_dry_run.txt: `Pioneer dry run: bundle with crossflash`

removed with the real-engine Pioneer execute goldens: these drove the
post-backup stages with a hand-made installed backup, which the real engine
cannot produce, because it always captures the backup itself. They were
dropped from both sets:

* pioneer_flash_bundle_failures.txt: `Pioneer flash_bundle: no installed
  backup` (the engine refuses to execute without a saved backup),
  `Pioneer flash_bundle: installed backup is garbage` (the capture builds the
  archive itself) and `Pioneer flash_bundle: installed backup is Normal-only`
  (the capture always reads the Kernel first and stops without it, so it never
  saves a Normal-only backup)

**Moved scenarios.** The Pioneer scenarios that ran the post-backup stages
through a test copy (`authorize`, then `execute` with an ungated grant) now
run the real `engine::flash` end to end on `Ud04Drive`, which replays the
UD04 backup fixture for the pre-flash backup and then takes the OEM update.
Both sets were re-recorded:

* flash_execute.txt `Pioneer flash_bundle: plain update (no kernel patch)` and
  `… update with kernel restoration pass` are now pioneer_execute.txt
  `Pioneer execute: Kernel+Normal update` and `… with kernel restoration pass`
* pioneer_flash_bundle_failures.txt `Pioneer flash_bundle: <case>` is now
  `Pioneer execute: <case>`; the dry-run request is `Pioneer flash: dry-run
  request`

**Added scenarios.** `pioneer_execute.txt` and `pioneer_execute_tty.txt` run
the real Pioneer execute path: Kernel+Normal, restoration pass, Normal-only,
a Normal for another Kernel tag (refused after the backup) and a disc
inserted after the backup, in process with consent given up front (v0.11.2:
its captured-output confirmation), plus the CLI's terminal confirmation in a
child process: stdin not a TTY, and (unix only) a pseudo-terminal answering
`y` or `n`. Both sets were recorded with the same harness; the v0.11.2 child
answers v0.11.2's own `confirm_proceed`. flash_execute.txt gained MediaTek
execute refusals (MT1939 image, raw drive read). The v0.11.2 copy of the
harness needed only COMPAT shims and the pinned `libc` dev-dependency; no
v0.11.2 code changed.

`pioneer_confirm_prompt.txt` (phase 4) covers the CLI
confirmation prompt, TTY and not. Its baseline was recorded at the v0.11.2 tag
with the same harness, driving v0.11.2's `confirm_with` (made `pub(crate)` in
the throwaway worktree, a visibility-only COMPAT change); the current file
drives `engine::flash` and the CLI's prompt core and is byte-identical.

`pioneer_corpus.txt` (`src/golden_corpus_tests.rs`) runs the real engine on
one mock drive per Pioneer family of an OEM package corpus: backup, dry run,
same-version, downgrade, upgrade and Normal-only flashes, and recovery. The
packages are pinned by SHA-256 in `pioneer_corpus_subset.tsv`; recording
needs the corpus. Both sets were recorded with the same file, its v0.11.2
copy changing only COMPAT lines. All 145 families the corpus can mock are
pinned. Earlier snapshots differed for the P2 authorization order and P3
refusals of product labels without a `BD-` prefix. The current P10 executor
uses decoded firmware and receiver evidence, so those labels alone no
longer prevent a flash. OEM Recovery with supplied Current firmware uses
the same evidence; probing an unsupported OEM identity without Current
remains refused. P11 records the prior Normal preparation fixes now
refreshed in this corpus. The exact changes and remaining refusals are
listed by scenario below; the historical snapshots are unchanged.

**New golden files.** `mtk_family_gate.txt` (M-FAM) records the MediaTek
hardware-family gate, which v0.11.2 does not have (it flashed a same-model
image from another board line, e.g. a BH16NS40 JB8 build onto a JB7 drive),
so it has no baseline and `golden_parity_with_0_11_2` skips it by name
(`NEW_SINCE_0_11_2`). Its six scenarios run the real engine: a same-line,
same-build reflash for a JB7 and a JB8 drive (the OEM session, unchanged),
both cross-line directions and an unknown family on either side, refused
before any write.

Regenerate the skeleton after an intentional change with
`FREEMKV_BLESS_INTENDED=1 cargo test -p freemkv-flash golden_parity`, then set
the `reason:` of any `UNCLASSIFIED` section by hand.
